q1: Can we use dropout 0.1 within our loss and step-time budgets?
Next: rb experiment add "<what would answer it>" -q q1 --hypothesis "<what you expect>"

$ rb experiment add 'dropout 0.1 vs none' --id drop -q q1 --hypothesis 'Dropout 0.1 lowers val_loss' -m 'less co-adaptation' --baseline none --candidate p01 --varies dropout --note 'assumes the validation split stayed fixed'
Experiment drop: dropout 0.1 vs none · none (baseline) vs p01 (candidate) · varies dropout · under q1
hypothesis: Dropout 0.1 lowers val_loss (why: less co-adaptation)
Planned: nothing in the record tests it yet, and it shows as a planned direction until its first run or analysis.
Made 2 variants: none (baseline), p01 (candidate); a setting of one is rb spec set drop none.<setting> <value>.
drop declares it varies dropout, but no variant has a value for it yet; give each variant its own: rb spec set drop <variant>.dropout <value> --source <file#key>
Next: rb spec set drop --from <config.yaml> --keys "<the keys that define it>"  ·  rb criterion add "<what it should show>" -e drop -q q1 --metric <name> --at-most <x>
$ rb spec set drop --from configs/train.json --keys optim.lr
drop/seed · per-run: each run gives its own, with --set seed=<value> on rb run add

$ rb criterion add 'Dropout 0.1 costs at most 0.02 val_loss' -e drop --metric change.val_loss --at-most 0.02 --min-n 3 --noise 0.01 --id c1 -q q1 --when-met 'Dropout 0.1 meets the declared validation-loss budget.'
c1: Dropout 0.1 costs at most 0.02 val_loss
Next: rb run add drop none.val_loss=<value> p01.val_loss=<value> --set seed=<value> --command "..."
$ rb criterion add 'Dropout keeps a step under 21 ms' -e drop --metric p01.step_ms --at-most 21 --min-n 3 --id c2 -q q1 --when-met 'Dropout 0.1 meets the declared step-time budget.'
c2: Dropout keeps a step under 21 ms
Next: rb run add drop p01.step_ms=<value> --set seed=<value> --command "..."
$ rb freeze drop -m 'before the runs that count'
drop frozen: spec ab5436635dfa · before the runs that count
